solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fusspot cries out, interrupting someone at the keyboard

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been knocked into disorder and must be rearranged
something interrupting breaks into the middle of another word, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a pianist plays at a keyboard

explanation.surface: A fussy person shouts out and interrupts a musician who is playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' reads as shouting aloud in the surface but signals rearrangement; the jumble lands after the musician's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A precisianist is a stickler for strict precision, exactly the kind of punctilious person called a fusspot.

clue.text: Invader beginning with cunning movement that brings protest

blocks.note: the Huns invaded the Roman Empire
a germ is the beginning from which something grows
arch means slyly knowing

explanation.surface: An invading army starts a crafty manoeuvre that provokes resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks military in the surface, but the definition is a march of the unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunger march is a procession of unemployed or poor people walking to demand relief, a protest movement.

clue.text: Arrangement (as it is mostly!) for trucks

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
the parenthesis says the answer is the arrangement as it stands, but read from the other end

blocks.note: a setup is an arrangement

explanation.surface: A playful aside about an arrangement made for some lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: SETUP loses its last letter and is read backwards to give UTES; the cheeky exclamation claims the answer is that arrangement, mostly, as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Ute is Australian shorthand for a utility vehicle, a small pick-up truck.

clue.text: Slight bow with formality indicates lack of success

blocks.note: a nod is a slight bow of the head
ice means cold, stiff reserve

explanation.surface: A curt little bow and stiff manner shows someone has failed to get anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: No dice is an informal idiom meaning that an attempt has failed or a request is refused.

clue.text: Wheel embedded in soil — what it can't do?

definitions.text: Wheel embedded in soil — what it can't do?

indicators.note: something embedded in another thing is set firmly inside it

blocks.note: a wheel is round, like the letter O
ground is earth or soil

explanation.surface: A wheel stuck fast in the earth cannot turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the O sits inside GROUND, and a wheel stuck in the ground cannot go round.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round is to rotate, which is exactly what a wheel jammed in the earth is prevented from doing.

clue.text: Fast female with name for pursuing lusty man

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so these pieces come after the other one

blocks.note: a ram is slang for a lecherous man
a girl's name
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A quick woman, giving her name, chases after a lecherous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quick or racy, but it is a noun: a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim holy month during which believers abstain from food in daylight hours.

clue.text: Governor losing heart in desolate Scottish area

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: a mudir was a local governor in the Ottoman Empire and Egypt

explanation.surface: A governor feels dispirited out in some bleak Scottish wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Muir is the Scots form of moor, a bleak open stretch of upland heath.

clue.text: Daughter keeps calm? The opposite, morning and afternoon

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it inside
the opposite flips who holds whom, so the calm word holds the daughter

blocks.note: first part of allay, to calm
D is the abbreviation for daughter
rest of allay

explanation.surface: A daughter stays calm — or rather doesn't — through the whole day.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLAY means calm; it is ALLAY that contains D, not the reverse that the surface states first.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning and afternoon together cover the whole of the daytime, which is what all day means.

clue.text: Tree turning yellow and pale

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read the other way

blocks.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
wan means pale

explanation.surface: A tree whose leaves turn yellow and pale in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree with bright red berries.

clue.text: Peter suffering with another bug

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter is ill, along with someone else, with a stomach bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' reads as an illness that Peter has caught, but here it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Heteropterans are the true bugs, an insect suborder including shield bugs and water boatmen.

clue.text: Chief scoundrel we found in Glasgow

blocks.note: a rat is a contemptible person
oo is a Scots form of we

explanation.surface: A leading villain and his gang turn up in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in Glasgow' flags the Scots dialect word for the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratoo, or ratu, is a title for a Fijian chief or local headman.

clue.text: Part of plant offering unusual camouflage, fine silver being invisible

indicators.note: pieces that become invisible vanish from the word
unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A plant disguises itself so cleverly that fine silver vanishes from view.
explanation.definitionFit: A caulome is the stem or axis of a plant considered as a structural part.

clue.text: Very much at home when entertaining a fellow from Ireland

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest takes it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: miles means by a great deal, as in miles better
first letter of in, at home
taken as written
rest of in, at home

explanation.surface: Someone very comfortable at home is hosting an Irish visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Milesians are the legendary Irish descended from King Milesius, so the word means an Irishman.

clue.text: River with a road round that has bench in recess

indicators.note: turned round means the pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A riverside road curves round a parliament that has gone into recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bench in recess' suggests judges or MPs on holiday, but the recess is an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An exedra is a semicircular recess or alcove with a built-in seat, common in classical architecture.

clue.text: French poet-composer arranging overture

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French composer is scoring the overture to a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranging' works as musical arranging in the surface, fitting the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouvères were medieval poet-musicians of northern France, counterparts of the southern troubadours.

clue.text: Old cat is what to expect by valley

blocks.note: par is the expected standard, as in golf
a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: An elderly cat is about what you would expect to find down in the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Pardale is an obsolete word for a panther or leopard, a big spotted cat.

clue.text: One border in which copper is seen to be tetchy

indicators.note: something in which another thing is seen holds it inside

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
first part of rand, a border or strip
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rest of rand

explanation.surface: At one frontier post the policeman looks short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal. A rand is a strip of border, as on a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Iracund is a rare word for irascible, prone to anger, and so tetchy.

clue.text: Looking back, some children accepted cruel teacher?

indicators.note: looking back means reading from right to left
some of the words means only a run of their letters is taken

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Pupils remember, looking back, how they put up with a harsh schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters RENAC sit across childREN ACcepted; read backwards they give CANER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caner is someone who beats with a cane, as harsh schoolmasters once did; the question mark flags the description.

clue.text: God about to become irritated

indicators.note: turned about means the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A deity is on the point of losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' alone is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore can mean annoyed or aggrieved, as in feeling sore about a slight.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill stands on head clutching horse — nothing to it!

indicators.note: standing on its head in a down clue turns the word upside down
clutching means holding something within
added to it means attached at the end

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
an Arab is a breed of horse
zero looks like O

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill Cody performs a headstand while gripping his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffalo Bill' looks like Mr Cody, but Buffalo is the definition and Bill a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The carabao is the domesticated water buffalo of the Philippines.

clue.text: No longer endure a run on the field

blocks.note: taken as written
in cricket a bye is a run scored without the ball being hit

explanation.surface: A tired fielder can bear no more of running about on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bye is a run taken when the ball passes the batsman and the keeper without being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Abye is an archaic verb meaning to suffer or pay the penalty for, so endure in an obsolete sense.

clue.text: Taxi reversing! Anxiety in old-fashioned warning to get back

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
care means worry

explanation.surface: A taxi backing up causes alarm, prompting a shouted warning to stand back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' fits the taxi in the surface and does the same job in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccare is a Shakespearean exclamation meaning go back or stand back, an archaic warning.

clue.text: Retrospective month for acting establishment

indicators.note: retrospective means looking backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: Adar is a month of the Jewish calendar

explanation.surface: A month-long retrospective is staged at a drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Academy of Dramatic Art is a famous school that trains actors.

clue.text: Animal with something wing-like gathers speed shortly

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter is removed
to gather something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: an ala is a wing-like part in anatomy or botany
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A creature with wing-like limbs quickly picks up speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated South American camelid kept for its fine wool.

clue.text: Weak and knowing defeat

blocks.note: W stands for weak, as in the weak force of particle physics
hip means in the know, aware

explanation.surface: Someone feeble yet aware that they are being beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip is to beat thoroughly, so it serves as a verb meaning to defeat.

clue.text: Turn pale, being struck in congested metropolis

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: first part of wen, the Great Wen being Cobbett's name for crowded London
hit means struck
end of wen

explanation.surface: Someone goes white after being hit in a crowded city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Wen was William Cobbett's nickname for London, a swollen, congested city.
explanation.definitionFit: To whiten is to become white, and so to blanch or go pale.

clue.text: Grandparent's member of a "lower" class? Lower no more

blocks.note: aval means relating to a grandparent
E is the lowest social grade in the UK classification

explanation.surface: A grandparent belongs to a lower social class, and is no longer down.
explanation.walkthrough: UK socio-economic grades run from A down to E, so E is the lowest class.
explanation.definitionFit: Avale is an obsolete verb meaning to lower or let fall, hence lower no more in use.

clue.text: Oil — a sailor brings tons aboard

indicators.note: bringing something aboard takes it inside the vessel
aboard means inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tons
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman loads tonnes of oil onto the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is a fragrant essential oil distilled from flowers, especially rose petals.

clue.text: Break the law again, offering cry to hounds

blocks.note: first meaning: cheat once more, split as re- plus cheat
second meaning: a horn call recalling hounds in hunting

explanation.surface: A repeat offender shouts at dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a made-up re- word; the second is the real word, a hunting term.
explanation.definitionFit: A recheat is the hunting horn signal sounded to call the hounds back together.

clue.text: Style of court action that could bring penalty

indicators.note: what a word could bring about is something remade from its letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of legal action that might lead to a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'penalty' suggest a law court, but this court is for tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Netplay is the tennis style of playing volleys near the net, a way of acting on court.

clue.text: Gents maybe getting tense — prize in sight

blocks.note: the Gents is a men's toilet, a loo
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A man in the toilets grows tense as a reward comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gents is the British name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is plunder or booty, a prize seized and visible for the taking.

clue.text: Female attire seen in the south of France

blocks.note: first meaning: a skirt or coat of mid-calf length
second meaning: the French name for the southern region

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman's outfit spotted on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a mid-calf garment, and le Midi is the French term for the southern part of the country.

clue.text: Mother faces row for being more friendly

indicators.note: facing something means standing in front of it, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: ma is mother
a tier is a row or rank

explanation.surface: Mum confronts a quarrel in order to be kinder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument, but here it is a line of seats. Matey means pally, and this is its comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Matier is the comparative of matey, meaning chummier, so it means more friendly.

clue.text: Fuel provided by a firm given external mark of approval

indicators.note: being given something on the outside means wrapped inside it

blocks.note: first part of seal, a mark of approval
taken as written
Co is the abbreviation for company
end of seal

explanation.surface: A company supplies fuel stamped with an official seal of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Seacoal is an old name for mineral coal, originally coal brought by sea, burnt as fuel.

clue.text: Life form assistant knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over lies the other way up, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: an aider is a helper

explanation.surface: A living creature's helper gets bowled over.
explanation.definitionFit: A redia is a larval stage of a parasitic fluke, a particular form of organism.

clue.text: What makes creation get out of control, creating monsters?

definitions.text: What makes creation get out of control, creating monsters?

indicators.note: letters out of control run wild and settle in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what lets creation run wild and produce monsters.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well as giving the letters: something teratogenic makes development go wrong, producing deformities.
explanation.definitionFit: Teratogenic describes an agent that causes malformations in an embryo, literally producing monsters.
